issues.legal_issue: A female heir who inherits a defined interest in joint family property does not automatically cease to be a member of the family unless she chooses to separate.
material_facts: A male member of a Mitakshara joint family died after the Hindu Succession Act came into force, and his interest devolved on his son, wife, and mother under Section 6.
The female heirs’ interests in the property became fixed, but they continued to live together and enjoy the family properties with the surviving male member.
Neither female heir took action to separate from the family, and the asserted family settlement was not pressed.
issues.conclusion: The female heirs did not cease to be members of the joint family merely because their interests in the property became fixed on the male member’s death; their separation required their volition.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6 and Explanation I of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the notional partition is a legal fiction used to determine the deceased coparcener’s interest and the heirs’ shares; it cannot be extended to deem a female heir separated from the family without her volition. A Hindu joint family may include female members and need not own joint family property. The Court explained Gurupad Khandappa Magdum v. Hirabai Khandappa Magdum, [1978] 3 SCR 761, as addressing the shares due when a female heir sues for partition, not automatic cessation of family membership, and relied on Gowli Buddanna v. Commissioner of Income Tax, [1966] 3 SCR 224, Sitabai v. Ram Chandra, [1970] 2 SCR 1, and N. V. Narendranath v. Commissioner of Wealth Tax, [1969] 3 SCR 882.

rule.if: agricultural_ceiling_proceeding and female_heir_inherited_defined_interest and notional_partition_used_to_calculate_interest and no_voluntary_separation and family_members_continued_jointly

predicates.agricultural_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns the application of an agricultural land ceiling to a family’s landholding.
predicates.female_heir_inherited_defined_interest: A female member inherited a defined interest in family property when a male family member died.
predicates.notional_partition_used_to_calculate_int: A notional partition was used to calculate the deceased member’s interest and the heirs’ shares.
predicates.no_voluntary_separation: The female heir did not choose or take action to separate from the family.
predicates.family_members_continued_jointly: The surviving family members continued living together or holding and enjoying the family property together.

issues.definition: When a female heir inherits a defined interest calculated by a notional partition but does not choose to separate and the family continues jointly, she remains a family member.

issues.legal_issue: A family member’s separate holding of land does not by itself end that person’s membership of the family or entitle that person to a separate ceiling unit.
material_facts: The heirs’ interests in the family property had become fixed after the male member’s death.
The respondents relied on the separate interests to claim individual ceiling units, but the alleged family settlement was not pressed.
The Court considered the proviso to Section 6 of the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961, concerning a member who separately held land.
issues.conclusion: The proviso to Section 6 of the Ceiling Act applied only when determining an increase in the family’s ceiling area; it did not establish that a member holding separate land ceased to be a family member for all purposes or gained a separate ceiling unit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(11) and 2(22) of the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961 define family and person for the Act’s purposes. The proviso to Section 6 is limited to determining the additional ceiling area available to a family with more than five members and does not generally remove a separate landholder from family membership. The Court’s discussion of joint-family membership also relied on Gowli Buddanna, Sitabai, and N. V. Narendranath.

predicates.agricultural_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns the application of an agricultural land ceiling to a family’s landholding.
predicates.family_member_holds_land_separately: A person who is a member of a family holds some land separately.

issues.definition: In an agricultural ceiling proceeding, a family member’s separate landholding alone does not end family membership or create a separate ceiling unit.

issues.legal_issue: Members of a family treated as one person under the agricultural ceiling scheme are collectively limited to one ceiling unit when they remain members of the same family.
material_facts: The surviving son, his mother, and his grandmother continued to hold the family properties together after the male member’s death.
No family settlement or voluntary separation was established.
The Ceiling Act defined a person to include a family, and the administrative determination allowing only one ceiling unit had been affirmed by the Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The surviving family members were together entitled to retain only one unit of the ceiling area, and the administrative order affirmed by the Tribunal was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(11) and 2(22) of the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961 include a family within the definition of person, so a family cannot hold more than one ceiling unit merely because members have individually fixed interests. Sections 3 and 4 provide for the ceiling and treatment of land held in excess of it. The Court also relied on the principles concerning the continued existence of a joint family discussed in Gowli Buddanna, Sitabai, and N. V. Narendranath.

predicates.agricultural_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns the application of an agricultural land ceiling to a family’s landholding.
predicates.family_members_remained_joint: The relevant family members continued to hold and enjoy the family property together without separating.
predicates.ceiling_scheme_counts_family_as_person: The applicable ceiling scheme treats a family as a person for determining the permitted landholding.

issues.definition: When family members remain joint in an agricultural ceiling proceeding and the ceiling scheme counts the family as a person, they are collectively entitled to one ceiling unit.
